sources.note: Awarding body's (UNESCO) own page, 'UNESCO/Poland Co-Sponsored Fellowships in Engineering 2025 edition', Last update 13 June 2025. States the 2025 edition is closed; no currently-open cycle.

The record's cited official_source_url (Polish government / NAWA study portal). Loads but is stale: still describes the 2023 edition (30 fellowships, 71 invited states, deadline 9 June 2023, BSc allowance 1500 PLN), materially contradicting the record. Not the awarding body itself.
Host institution (UNESCO Chair for Science, Technology and Engineering at AGH University of Krakow). News listing shows only 2025 editions as the latest for this programme.

UNESCO fellowships hub, updated 28 Sep 2026. Lists 28 UNESCO/Poland Engineering fellowships with no open call for it (only the UNESCO/Japan Keizo Obuchi call is shown open, until 30 Sep 2026). Read via search-result content.

Sibling UNESCO/Poland Archaeology & Conservation programme (different record); shows a 2026-2027 edition (deadline extended to 8 June 2026), confirming the Engineering page is the stale one by comparison. Read via search-result content.

awarding_body.detail: The UNESCO page is genuinely the awarding organisation's own. The programme is offered by UNESCO, co-sponsored with the Polish National Commission for UNESCO and hosted by the UNESCO Chair at AGH University of Krakow. The record's awarding_body value 'Gov.Pl' is imprecise and should be corrected (see notes_for_reviewer).
awarding_body.quote: the Polish National Commission for UNESCO and the UNESCO Chair for Science, Technology, and Engineering at the AGH University of Krakow (Poland) are placing at the disposal of UNESCO twenty-eight (28) fellowships

deadline.detail: The published deadline matches the record ('by Monday 26 May 2025, Midnight Paris time at the latest') but it is the deadline of the 2025 edition, which the page states is now closed; as of 12 October 2026 no currently-open 2026/2027 cycle is published, so the record cannot be verified as open. The record's own cited URL is still older, showing a 9 June 2023 deadline (2023 edition).
deadline.quote: The 2025 edition of this Programme is closed for applications.

eligibility.detail: 57 invited Member States matches the record's '57 states in the 2025 edition'; eligibility requires a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree plus UNESCO nomination through the candidate's own National Commission (individual applications not accepted); Annex III governs per-field and per-region restrictions. Note: the record's cited study.gov.pl URL shows '71 invited Member States' for its superseded 2023 edition, which conflicts with the record's 57; UNESCO's current 2025 figure (57) is correct.

funding.detail: Fully Funded as a comprehensive package: free tuition for 6 months; international airfare and health insurance covered by UNESCO; a monthly allowance intended to cover all living expenses and accommodation (1800 PLN BSc / 2200 PLN MSc); a one-time arrival allowance (1800/2200 PLN); and a one-time US$120 pocket allowance.
funding.quote: This allowance is intended to cover all living expenses and accommodation in Poland.

degree_levels.detail: Candidates must already hold a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree; the award is a 6-month individual research programme in Science, Technology and Engineering at AGH Krakow. Matches the record's 'Bachelor's, Master's, PhD'.
degree_levels.quote: Certified copies (in English) of Bachelor's, Master's Degree or PhD degree obtained

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: by Monday 26 May 2025, Midnight Paris time at the latest (2025 edition - now closed)
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: UNESCO/Poland Co-Sponsored Fellowships in ENGINEERING: latest published edition is 2025 (28 fellowships at AGH Krakow; deadline 26 May 2025) and it is CLOSED; upstream Last update 13 June 2025 with no 2026/2027 call yet. The record's cited study.gov.pl mirror is stale (still shows the 2023 edition: 30 fellowships, 71 states, deadline 9 June 2023, BSc allowance 1500 PLN) - prefer the UNESCO page. Do not confuse with the separate UNESCO/Poland Archaeology & Conservation programme, which has its own 2026-2027 edition. awarding_body should be corrected from 'Gov.Pl' to 'UNESCO (co-sponsored with the Polish National Commission for UNESCO / Government of Poland)'. Because the 2025 cycle closed with no open successor, the record must not be shown to users as currently open/active; re-check for a new engineering call before reinstating active.

notes_for_reviewer: The record's factual 2025 data matches UNESCO's page exactly (57 invited states, deadline 26 May 2025, eligibility by National-Commission nomination, fully-funded package, Bachelor's/Master's/PhD prerequisite), so this is not a fabricated record - but its verification_status 'active' is contradicted: the only documented cycle (2025) is closed and no currently-open engineering cycle exists as of 12 Oct 2026, so it must leave 'active'. Its cited official_source_url (study.gov.pl) is stale and points to a materially different 2023 edition. Two items need a human decision: (1) whether/how to present a closed-cycle scholarship on a catalogue that currently brands it active/open; and (2) correct awarding_body from 'Gov.Pl' to UNESCO / Polish National Commission for UNESCO. A future re-check should watch the UNESCO page for a 2026/2027 engineering edition.
